items.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021
items.q: Jimmy Smith, it was like a regular keyboard, electric keyboard.

ctx.x: Yeah. They finally gave me credit for — I think — because they sent me, years later, “On the Corner” they gave me credit for “Ife” I think. But it was, like you say, shoot, when I first got the call to do a Miles I think they was working on something and I walked into the studio and there’s three keyboards. So I assumed that I was supposed to wait my turn. I didn’t know — because back then Miles was really experimenting. And so I was standing up against the wall and Miles walked over and said what the bleep you…

Jimmy Smith, it was like a regular keyboard, electric keyboard. So he said, “I want you to play that.” So I said, “Well Miles, I never played it.” He said, “Oh that’s fantastic.” I said, “Well Miles, can I take it home and practice?” “Oh no, no, no.” So Monk, I had to learn the keyboard and play, and create on stage. But that’s what Miles wanted. He’d get mad if you didn’t come up with anything creative each night. And you know that’s hard for somebody that wants you to really create and be yourself.
That’s a great story. So this morning I was doing a little ear training.
